## Calculation

Given:

- Tensile force: \(F=90\,\text{kN}=90{,}000\,\text{N}\)
- Pin diameter: \(d=18\,\text{mm}\)
- allowable tensile stress: \(\sigma_{\text{allow}}=155\,\text{MPa}=155\,\text{N/mm}^2\)
- Length: \(L=1.5\,\text{m}\)
- Density: \(\rho=7850\,\text{kg/m}^3\)

Assumptions:

- The hole diameter equals the pin diameter, 18 mm.
- The critical tensile section is the net section through the hole:
  \[
  A_{\text{net}}=(w-d)t
  \]
- Stress is the average tensile stress on that net section; no additional stress-concentration factor is specified.
- Catalogue mass is based on the gross section area, \(A=wt\), as stated in the Plainflat catalogue. The small hole volume is not deducted.

Stress and mass are calculated from:

\[
\sigma=\frac{F}{A_{\text{net}}}
\]

\[
m=\rho A L
=\rho\left(A\times10^{-6}\right)(1.5)
\]

| Bar | Net area calculation (mm²) | Stress calculation (MPa) | Mass calculation (kg) | Result |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---|
| PF-60x10 | \((60-18)(10)=420\) | \(90{,}000/420=214.3\) | \(7850(600\times10^{-6})(1.5)=7.065\) | Fails stress |
| PF-70x10 | \((70-18)(10)=520\) | \(90{,}000/520=173.1\) | \(7850(700\times10^{-6})(1.5)=8.243\) | Fails stress |
| PF-80x10 | \((80-18)(10)=620\) | \(90{,}000/620=145.2\) | \(7850(800\times10^{-6})(1.5)=9.420\) | Passes |
| PF-80x12 | \((80-18)(12)=744\) | \(90{,}000/744=121.0\) | \(7850(960\times10^{-6})(1.5)=11.304\) | Passes |

All four bars satisfy the minimum width of 40 mm, minimum thickness of 6 mm, and the 20 kg mass limit. Of the bars that also satisfy the stress limit, PF-80x10 has the lower mass:

\[
9.420\,\text{kg}<11.304\,\text{kg}
\]

Therefore, the lightest compliant Plainflat bar is **PF-80x10**, with a net-section tensile stress of **145.2 MPa**, below the 155 MPa limit.

Assumptions used: 80 °C Solvex-80 properties apply; all pressures are absolute; tank free-surface velocity is negligible; no catalogue interpolation to 18 L/s is made, so a pump is acceptable only if its catalogue flow/head meet or exceed the duty and its catalogue NPSHr satisfies the margin. Suction-bore velocity head is not an extra subtraction because NPSH is total suction head above vapour pressure.

Fluid data at 80 °C:  
\[
\rho=820\ \text{kg/m}^3,\quad p_v=45.0\ \text{kPa}=45000\ \text{Pa}
\]
Free-surface pressure:  
\[
p_0=101.3\ \text{kPa}=101300\ \text{Pa}
\]
Pressure head above vapour pressure:  
\[
\frac{p_0-p_v}{\rho g}
=\frac{101300-45000}{820(9.81)}
=\frac{56300}{8044.2}
=6.9988\ \text{m}
\]
Flooded-suction static head and suction loss:  
\[
\text{NPSH}_a=6.9988+2.5-1.2=8.2988\ \text{m}\approx 8.30\ \text{m}
\]
Suction velocity check:  
\[
A=\frac{\pi(0.200)^2}{4}=0.031416\ \text{m}^2,\quad
V=\frac{0.018}{0.031416}=0.573\ \text{m/s},\quad
\frac{V^2}{2g}=0.0167\ \text{m}
\]
This velocity head cancels in the free-surface-to-suction total-head equation, so \(\text{NPSH}_a\) remains \(8.2988\) m.

Required NPSH margin:
- H-210: \(1.15(10.0)=11.50\) m → fails, \(8.2988<11.50\)
- H-240: \(1.15(8.5)=9.775\) m → fails, \(8.2988<9.775\)
- H-280: \(1.15(6.4)=7.360\) m → passes, \(8.2988\ge7.360\)
- H-320: \(1.15(5.5)=6.325\) m → passes

All four catalogue points meet/exceed the 18 L/s and 22 m duty, all have shaft power below 15 kW, and all are rated to 120 °C. The NPSH-compliant choices are H-280 at EUR 4550 and H-320 at EUR 5900; therefore the cheapest compliant pump is H-280. Its catalogue point is 24 L/s and 30 m, exceeding the specified 18 L/s and 22 m duty.

Assumptions used: three-phase feeder; 400 V is line-to-line; 75 kVA is three-phase kVA; the reactor is series-connected; with negligible winding resistance, the first-order voltage-magnitude drop for lagging load is \(\Delta V \approx I X \sin\phi\).

Load current:

\[
I_L=\frac{75{,}000}{\sqrt{3}\cdot 400}=108.253\text{ A}
\]

Power factor:

\[
\cos\phi=0.8 \Rightarrow \sin\phi=0.6
\]

Catalogue reactance base:

\[
Z_{\text{base}}=\frac{400^2}{100{,}000}=1.6\ \Omega,\qquad X=1.6x
\]

Voltage-drop percent:

\[
\Delta V\%=
100\frac{\sqrt{3} I_L X\sin\phi}{400}
=100\frac{\sqrt{3}(108.253)(1.6x)(0.6)}{400}
=45x
\]

**Final conclusion:** select **Lumenford Bay B-320**. Its rated current is 461.9 A, above the 108.253 A load current; its calculated voltage drop is 2.475% \(\le 3.0\%\); and at EUR 4500 it is cheaper than the other compliant reactor, B-500 at EUR 6100. # Servo Sizing — Turntable Indexer

## Step 1: Motion profile (output shaft)

Symmetric triangular profile: accelerate 0.20 s, decelerate 0.20 s, total angle θ = 90° = π/2 = 1.5708 rad.

- Peak output speed: ω_pk = 2θ/t = 2(1.5708)/0.40 = **7.854 rad/s** (= 75 rpm)
- Output angular acceleration: α = ω_pk/0.20 = 4θ/t² = **39.27 rad/s²**

## Step 2: Torque required at the table (output shaft)

Coulomb friction (4.0 N·m) opposes motion in both halves; it adds to the accel torque and subtracts from the braking torque. Dwell torque = 0 (no gravity/process load; static friction holds).

- Accel: T_acc = Jα + T_f = 1.20(39.27) + 4.0 = 47.12 + 4.0 = **+51.12 N·m**
- Decel: T_dec = −Jα + T_f = −47.12 + 4.0 = **−43.12 N·m**
- Dwell (1.6 s): **0 N·m**

## Step 3: Reflect to motor shaft (lossless gearing)

T_motor = (J_m + J_L/N²)·N·α ± T_f/N; motor speed = N·ω_pk = 75N rpm.

**Check in cost order:**

**A40 (€470, N=20):** T_acc = (0.00015 + 1.20/400)(785.4) + 0.20 = 2.474 + 0.20 = **2.674 N·m > 2.40 peak → FAIL**

**A20 (€610, N=10):** T_acc = (0.00018 + 1.20/100)(392.7) + 0.40 = 4.783 + 0.40 = **5.183 N·m > 4.80 peak → FAIL**

**A60 (€690, N=30):**
- J_eq = 0.00025 + 1.20/900 = 0.001583 kg·m²; α_m = 30(39.27) = 1178.1 rad/s²
- T_acc = 0.001583(1178.1) + 4/30 = 1.865 + 0.133 = **1.999 N·m ≤ 3.50 ✓**
- T_dec = −1.865 + 0.133 = **−1.732 N·m**, |T| ≤ 3.50 ✓
- T_rms = √[(1.999²·0.2 + 1.732²·0.2 + 0·1.6)/2.0] = √[(3.995 + 3.000)(0.2)/2.0] = √0.6994 = **0.836 N·m ≤ 1.80 ✓**
- Speed: 30 × 7.854 = 235.6 rad/s = **2250 rpm ≤ 4000 ✓**
- Output torque: 51.12 N·m ≤ 90 ✓

**A60 passes all constraints.** (A80 also passes — T_acc = 1.906 N·m, T_rms = 0.809 N·m, 3000 rpm — but costs €880.)

## Conclusion

The two cheaper drives (A40, A20) both fail on motor peak torque during acceleration. The **A60** is the lowest-cost drive satisfying peak torque, rms torque, speed, and output-torque limits.

### Calculation

1. **Belt speed ratio**

For a belt drive, pulley pitch diameter is inversely proportional to speed:

\[
n_{\text{motor}}D_{\text{motor}}
=
n_{\text{process}}D_{\text{process}}
\]

\[
n_{\text{motor}}
=
3600\left(\frac{80}{240}\right)
=
1200\ \text{rpm}
\]

2. **Process-shaft power**

\[
\omega_{\text{process}}
=
\frac{2\pi(3600)}{60}
=
376.99\ \text{rad/s}
\]

\[
P_{\text{process}}
=
T_{\text{process}}\omega_{\text{process}}
=
15(376.99)
=
5654.9\ \text{W}
\]

3. **Required motor-shaft power**

Assuming the stated belt efficiency applies from motor shaft to process shaft:

\[
P_{\text{motor}}
=
\frac{P_{\text{process}}}{\eta}
=
\frac{5654.9}{0.96}
=
5890.5\ \text{W}
\]

4. **Required motor torque**

\[
\omega_{\text{motor}}
=
\frac{2\pi(1200)}{60}
=
125.66\ \text{rad/s}
\]

\[
T_{\text{motor,required}}
=
\frac{5890.5}{125.66}
=
46.88\ \text{N·m}
\]

Equivalently:

\[
T_{\text{motor,required}}
=
15\left(\frac{3600}{1200}\right)\frac{1}{0.96}
=
46.88\ \text{N·m}
\]

5. **Catalogue comparison**

| Model | Rated torque (N·m) | Torque adequate? | Current ≤16 A? | Mass ≤40 kg? | Price (EUR) |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| K-20 | 22 | No | Yes | Yes | 640 |
| K-40 | 40 | No | Yes | Yes | 910 |
| K-55 | 55 | Yes | Yes | Yes | 1280 |
| K-75 | 75 | Yes | No | No | 1710 |

The **K-55** is therefore the cheapest motor satisfying the torque, current, and mass requirements.

Assumptions used: steady 1-D radial conduction only; 1 m pipe length; jacket inner face is at the metal temperature, 200 °C; no contact resistance or air gap; jacket outer radius is pipe radius plus catalogue radial build; the given combined coefficient \(h=8.0\ \mathrm{W/m^2K}\) is constant on the outer jacket area; conductivity varies as stated, \(k(T)=k20[1+b(T-20)]\), with \(T\) in °C.

\[
r_i=\frac{120}{2}\text{ mm}=0.060\text{ m},\qquad r_o=r_i+t
\]

For outer jacket surface temperature \(T_s\), since \(k(T)\) is linear,

\[
T_m=\frac{200+T_s}{2},\qquad 
k_m=k20[1+b(T_m-20)]
\]

\[
q'_{\rm cond}=\frac{2\pi k_m(200-T_s)}{\ln(r_o/r_i)},\qquad
q'_{\rm ext}=h(2\pi r_o)(T_s-25)
\]

Solve \(q'_{\rm cond}=q'_{\rm ext}\) for the physical root \(25<T_s<200\).

Size/mass screening: KJ-70 is not admissible because 70 mm > 60 mm and 3.4 kg/m > 3.0 kg/m. KJ-20, KJ-40, and KJ-55 pass the size/mass screen and are checked thermally.

| jacket | \(r_o\) m | \(\ln(r_o/r_i)\) | solved \(T_s\) °C | \(k_m\) W/m·K | \(q'\) W/m | cost EUR/m | check |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---|
| KJ-20 | 0.080 | 0.287682 | 64.3805 | 0.0534628 | 158.358 | 14 | fails: \(q'>80\), \(T_s>50\) |
| KJ-40 | 0.100 | 0.510826 | 43.6791 | 0.0488318 | 93.8916 | 26 | fails: \(q'>80\) |
| KJ-55 | 0.115 | 0.650588 | 35.1058 | 0.0366825 | 58.4169 | 39 | passes all limits |

For the selected KJ-55: \(r_o=0.060+0.055=0.115\) m, \(\ln(r_o/r_i)=0.650588\), \(T_m=(200+35.1058)/2=117.5529\) °C, \(k_m=0.032[1+0.0015(117.5529-20)]=0.0366825\ \mathrm{W/mK}\). Then \(q'_{\rm cond}=58.4169\ \mathrm{W/m}\) and \(q'_{\rm ext}=8[2\pi(0.115)](35.1058-25)=58.4169\ \mathrm{W/m}\). Limits: 58.4169 < 80 W/m, 35.1058 < 50 °C, 55 mm < 60 mm, 2.6 kg/m < 3.0 kg/m.

Final conclusion: choose KJ-55. The cheaper KJ-20 and KJ-40 fail the 80 W/m duty; KJ-70 is excluded by radial build and mass.

Assumptions used: balanced 3-phase load; three single-core conductors in trefoil; 40 m is the one-way route length; catalogue R and X at 90 °C are used directly; lagging pf makes the reactive term additive; short-circuit check is adiabatic from 90 °C to 250 °C using the full 12 kA rms for 0.8 s, with no fault-current reduction credited along the feeder.

Voltage-drop limit:

\[
\Delta V_{\max}=0.03(400)=12\text{ V line-to-line}
\]

\[

\]

For a 3-phase feeder:

with \(I=180\) A and \(L=0.040\) km:

| Cable | Ampacity A | \(R\cos\phi+X\sin\phi\) Ω/km | Voltage drop V | Ampacity check | Voltage-drop check |

| V50 | 196 | 0.415888 | 5.19 | pass | pass |

Short-circuit withstand, adiabatic:

\[
\left(\frac{I}{S}\right)^2t=
\frac{\delta c}{\rho_{20}\alpha}
\ln\left(\frac{1+\alpha(250-20)}{1+\alpha(90-20)}\right)
\]

\[
k=\sqrt{\frac{(8890)(385)}{(1.724\times10^{-8})(0.00393)}
\ln\left(\frac{1.9039}{1.2751}\right)}
=142.3\ \text{A}\sqrt{\text{s}}/\text{mm}^2
\]

Required section:

\[
S_{\min}=\frac{I\sqrt{t}}{k}
=\frac{12000\sqrt{0.8}}{142.3}
=75.4\text{ mm}^2
\]

So V50 and V70 fail the short-circuit check; V95 is the smallest and lowest-cost cable that passes. Equivalently, for 0.8 s the allowable currents are about V50 = 7.96 kA, V70 = 11.14 kA, V95 = 15.11 kA, V120 = 19.09 kA.

Final conclusion: select **V95**. It satisfies ampacity \(301\ge180\) A, voltage drop \(2.98\le12\) V, and short-circuit requirement \(95\ge75.4\) mm², and it is cheaper than V120.
